headline: Nearly 7 lakh fail as SSC pass rate hits 19-year low
summary: The overall pass rate fell by 6.2 percentage points, with GPA-5 achievers also dropping to their lowest level since 2020.
details: Across all 11 boards, the combined pass rate for this year's SSC and equivalent exams was 62.25 percent. This marks a significant decline from the previous year, with nearly 7 lakh students failing to pass.

In the nine general education boards, the pass rate hit its lowest point since 2007. The number of students securing GPA-5 also reached its lowest level in six years, with 1,16,676 students achieving the top grade overall.

The results show a stark contrast in performance, as the number of institutions with a zero-pass rate more than doubled, rising from 134 to 312. Conversely, the number of schools with a 100 percent pass rate dropped from 984 to 669.

Education officials attributed the decline to weak performance in English and mathematics, as well as poor results among humanities students. A stricter evaluation process and tighter marking standards were also cited as contributing factors.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon defended the results, stating that students were awarded marks based on their actual performance and that marks cannot be awarded freely.

Despite the overall decline, female students continued to outperform males. Girls led boys in pass rates for 10 consecutive years and in GPA-5 achievements for nine years, with 66.68 percent of girls passing compared to 57.86 percent of boys.
The results were published with a delay, failing to meet the 60-day window after tests were completed. Minister Milon apologized for the delay, citing floods and other factors.

Across all 11 boards, the combined pass rate for this year's SSC and equivalent exams was 62.25 percent. This marks a significant decline from the previous year, with nearly 7 lakh students failing to pass.

In the nine general education boards, the pass rate hit its lowest point since 2007. The number of students securing GPA-5 also reached its lowest level in six years, with 1,16,676 students achieving the top grade overall.

The results show a stark contrast in performance, as the number of institutions with a zero-pass rate more than doubled, rising from 134 to 312. Conversely, the number of schools with a 100 percent pass rate dropped from 984 to 669.

Education officials attributed the decline to weak performance in English and mathematics, as well as poor results among humanities students. A stricter evaluation process and tighter marking standards were also cited as contributing factors.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon defended the results, stating that students were awarded marks based on their actual performance and that marks cannot be awarded freely.

Despite the overall decline, female students continued to outperform males. Girls led boys in pass rates for 10 consecutive years and in GPA-5 achievements for nine years, with 66.68 percent of girls passing compared to 57.86 percent of boys.

The results were published with a delay, failing to meet the 60-day window after tests were completed. Minister Milon apologized for the delay, citing floods and other factors.

headline: Tk 1.21 crore robbed from Uttara fuel pump in broad daylight
summary: A filling station official was hacked and a massive sum of money was stolen from a pump owned by the Prime Minister's cousin.
details: Gunmen robbed Tk 1.21 crore from a fuel pump in the Uttara area of Dhaka in broad daylight.
A filling station official was hacked during the incident, leaving them injured.
The fuel pump is reportedly owned by a cousin of the former Prime Minister.
Police are investigating the case to identify and apprehend the suspects.
